spatial_claims.claim: Circle with center O, radius OA; the side of the regular hexagon inscribed in the circle equals the radius OA
Point N lies on segment OA between O and A, cutting OA in extreme and mean ratio with ON as the greater segment and NA as the lesser segment

Isosceles triangle with vertex at O, equal sides equal to OA, vertex angle equal to one-fifth of two right angles (36 degrees); the base subtends 36 degrees at center so it is the decagon side; the base equals ON (greater segment of OA cut in EMR)
OA is cut in extreme and mean ratio with ON (decagon side) as greater segment and NA as lesser segment
Adding ON to OA produces a line OA+ON that is cut in extreme and mean ratio with OA as the greater segment (by 13.5)
The sum OA+ON equals hexagon side plus decagon side, and this whole line is cut in EMR with OA (hexagon side) as greater segment

configuration_map: Circle with center O and radius OA. Point N lies on segment OA between O and A, dividing OA in extreme and mean ratio: ON is the greater segment (approximately 0.618*OA), NA is the lesser segment (approximately 0.382*OA). The hexagon side equals OA (the radius). The decagon side equals ON (established via the Prop 4.10 isosceles triangle construction). The combined line OA+ON equals hexagon side + decagon side. All points are collinear on segment OA or its extension. No complex geometric configuration beyond points on a line and a standard circle with inscribed polygons.
pass_reason: The proof makes minimal spatial/geometric configuration claims, primarily involving segment equalities and golden ratio relationships along a single line. All spatial claims are mutually consistent: (1) N on segment OA with ON as greater segment is compatible with ON equaling the decagon side (verified numerically: decagon side = 2r*sin(18 degrees) approximately equals 0.618r, matching the golden ratio greater segment); (2) the application of Prop 13.5 correctly uses the established EMR cut to conclude the sum is in EMR; (3) the identification of hexagon side = OA and decagon side = ON is consistent throughout. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, and no conflicting positional requirements are present.
